title: Finite image from generic constancy on every prime closed subset
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $T$ be any set, and let $f:\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$ be any function, with no continuity assumption [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For an ideal $J\subseteq A$ write $V(J)=\{\mathfrak p:J\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$ and, for $b\in A$, write $D(b)=\{\mathfrak p:b\notin\mathfrak p\}$. Assume that for every prime ideal $I\subset A$ there are $b\in A\setminus I$ and $t\in T$ such that $f(\mathfrak p)=t$ for every $\mathfrak p\in V(I)\cap D(b)$. Then for every ideal $J\subseteq A$ the set $\{f(\mathfrak p):\mathfrak p\in V(J)\}$ is finite. In particular $f$ has finite image. The zero ring and the empty target set are allowed whenever such a function exists.

source.place: Tag 0ASY, lemma-generic-flatness-stratification, Noetherian-induction pattern; algebra.tex Tags 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic, and 00FR, lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components; abstract finite-image adaptation of the item proof steps 3 and 6.

proof.text: For an ideal $J$, put $F(J)=\{f(\mathfrak p):\mathfrak p\in V(J)\}$. Suppose some $F(J)$ is infinite and let $\Psi$ be the nonempty set of all such ideals. Regard ideals as $A$-submodules of the finite module $A$: the single element $1$ generates $A$, since $a=a\cdot1$ for every $a\in A$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-module-acc] gives $I\in\Psi$ maximal for inclusion. Thus $F(K)$ is finite for every ideal $K\supsetneq I$. Also $I\ne A$, since no proper prime ideal contains $1$, so $F(A)=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic, ascending-chain/maximal-element condition; agent-written finite-image argument.

proof.text: The ideal $I$ is prime. Indeed, otherwise its properness gives $a,c\notin I$ with $ac\in I$. Both $I+(a)$ and $I+(c)$ strictly contain $I$, so their $F$-sets are finite by maximality. A point $\mathfrak p\in V(I)$ is a prime ideal [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; hence $ac\in\mathfrak p$ forces $a\in\mathfrak p$ or $c\in\mathfrak p$. Conversely any prime containing either $I+(a)$ or $I+(c)$ contains $I$. Therefore $V(I)=V(I+(a))\cup V(I+(c))$ and $F(I)=F(I+(a))\cup F(I+(c))$, a finite union of two finite sets, a contradiction. Here prime means proper and satisfying $xy\in\mathfrak p\Rightarrow x\in\mathfrak p\text{ or }y\in\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic, ascending-chain/maximal-element condition; agent-written finite-image argument.

proof.text: Apply the hypothesis to the prime ideal $I$ just obtained. Choose $b\notin I$ and $t\in T$ with $f=t$ on $V(I)\cap D(b)$. The ideal $K=I+(b)$ strictly contains $I$, so $F(K)$ is finite. Every $\mathfrak p\in V(I)$ either omits $b$ and then has $f(\mathfrak p)=t$, or contains $b$ and then contains $K$. Consequently $F(I)\subseteq\{t\}\cup F(K)$ is finite, contradicting $I\in\Psi$. This uses only membership in $V$ and $D$, not continuity of $f$.

source.place: Tag 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic, ascending-chain/maximal-element condition; agent-written finite-image argument.

proof.text: There is thus no ideal $J$ with $F(J)$ infinite. This proves the stated assertion for every $J$. Every prime contains the zero ideal, so $V((0))=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $F((0))$ is the image of $f$, proving the final assertion. If $A$ is the zero ring, no proper prime exists and all these images are empty. If $T=\varnothing$ and a function $f$ exists, its domain is empty and the same conclusions hold.

lean.statement: theorem finite_image_of_generically_constant (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (T : Type v) (f : PrimeSpectrum A → T) : (∀ (I : Ideal A), I.IsPrime → ∃ b : A, b ∉ I ∧ ∃ t : T, ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, I ≤ p.asIdeal → b ∉ p.asIdeal → f p = t) → (∀ (J : Ideal A), (f '' {p : PrimeSpectrum A | J ≤ p.asIdeal}).Finite) ∧ (Set.range f).Finite
